clean_source_blocks.text: Armed men in Haiti have kidnapped the defence minister's chief of staff, the highest-ranking official to be kidnapped in the violence-wracked Caribbean country in recent years. Top security official James Boyard, who is also inspector general of Haiti's police, was seized in the island's capital Port-au-Prince on Thursday. Both the Associated Press news agency and the New York Times confirmed his abduction via sources, with the newspaper adding Boyard's wife and six-year-old daughter were also taken. A ransom has been requested, according to the New York Times, who cited a person familiar with the case. Boyard, a highly respected security expert, is chief of staff to Mario Andrésol who was appointed in March. He was tasked with helping rebuild Haiti's armed forces.

June 13 - Armed men in Haiti have kidnapped a senior ‌government and police official in ‌Port-au-Prince, the highest-ranking abduction in recent years in ​a country gripped by gang violence, according to media reports on Saturday. James Boyard, cabinet director at the Defense ‌Ministry and ⁠inspector general of Haiti's national police, was seized on Thursday ⁠in the Bourdon neighborhood, according to the Associated Press, which cited a ​person familiar ​with the ​case. Boyard is widely ‌regarded as a leading security expert and his abduction marks a significant escalation in the targeting of senior officials in Haiti, where gangs have ‌tightened their hold over ​the capital. Kidnappings have surged ​in Haiti ​as criminal groups expand ‌their influence, undermining government ​authority and ​worsening a deepening humanitarian and security crisis. Authorities have not publicly commented ​on efforts ‌to secure Boyard's release.
James Boyard's abduction is the highest-ranking abduction in the violence-wracked country in recent years, according to reports.

This event underscores the increasing threat posed by gangs, who have steadily tightened their grip on Haiti's capital. With kidnappings on the rise, the government's authority is being seriously undermined, contributing to a deepening humanitarian and security crisis. So far, authorities have not publicly revealed any efforts to secure Boyard's release, leaving the situation tense and unresolved. ---

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Armed men in Haiti have kidnapped the defence minister's chief of staff, the highest-ranking official to be kidnapped in the violence-wracked Caribbean country in recent years.

Top security official James Boyard, who is also inspector general of Haiti's police, was seized in the island's capital Port-au-Prince on Thursday.

Both the Associated Press news agency and the New York Times confirmed his abduction via sources, with the newspaper adding Boyard's wife and six-year-old daughter were also taken.

A ransom has been requested, according to the New York Times, who cited a person familiar with the case.

Boyard, a highly respected security expert, is chief of staff to Mario Andrésol who was appointed in March.

He was tasked with helping rebuild Haiti's armed forces.

Diego Da Rin, an analyst with the International Crisis Group, told AP news agency kidnappings are increasingly occurring in areas of Port-au-Prince once considered safe.

He added gang members have been kidnapping people with double nationalities and targeting public officials, which could mean they are trying to seek higher ransoms or possibly dissuade authorities from attacking gang-controlled areas where hostages are held.

Gang violence has ravaged the Caribbean country for years and the multinational police force sent to contain it has struggled to enter areas where gangs hold sway.

So far this year, gang-related violence has resulted in at least 2,310 deaths, 1,106 injuries and 99 kidnappings, according to the United Nations earlier this month.

It has also caused record levels of displacement with nearly 1.5 million people without a place to live, according to the latest figures released by the UN migration agency.

---

[Lähde: International Business Times Singapore]
Haiti Defense Ministry official James Boyard, who also serves as inspector general of the country's National Police, was kidnapped Thursday in Port-au-Prince, marking one of the most significant abductions involving a senior security official in recent years.

Boyard, also a political scientist, was tasked with helping rebuild Haiti's armed forces and had been assessing the National Police to implement reforms, making his abduction a direct blow to the country's fragile security infrastructure. It remains unclear who carried out the kidnapping or whether a ransom has been demanded.

At least 267 people were reported kidnapped in Haiti between December 2025 and February 2026, most of them men, according to a United Nations report. In 2025, 1,268 kidnappings were recorded, nearly 40% drop from 2,058 the previous year. Despite the declining numbers, Boyard's abduction signals that gang networks retain the capacity to target senior officials.

Local media reported Saturday that Boyard was abducted in Bourdon, one of the few areas in Port-au-Prince considered relatively safe. The neighborhood's reputation as a secure enclave made the abduction all the more alarming for Haitian authorities.

An estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince is controlled by a powerful gang coalition known as Viv Ansanm, which the U.S. designated as a foreign terrorist organization in May last year. The group has steadily tightened its grip over the capital, pushing government authority to the margins and making large parts of the city inaccessible.

"A person of this rank clearly has a fairly important security detail," said Diego Da Rin, an analyst with the International Crisis Group.

Haiti has experienced a series of high-profile kidnappings in recent years involving journalists, aid workers and foreign missionaries. However, the abduction of a serving government security official is relatively rare and may signal growing confidence among armed groups operating in the capital.

Authorities have not announced any arrests or provided additional details on efforts to locate Boyard. The case is expected to intensify scrutiny of the government's security strategy as officials continue to confront escalating gang influence across the country.

payload.title: Aseistetut miehet sieppasivat korkean turvallisuusviranomaisen Haitissa
payload.summary: Haitin puolustusministeriön kabinettijohtaja ja kansallisen poliisin ylitarkastaja James Boyard siepattiin Port-au-Princessä. Tapausta pidetään viime vuosien korkea-arvoisimpana sieppauksena maassa.
payload.content:
Aseistetut miehet ovat siepanneet Haitissa James Boyardin, joka toimii puolustusministeriön kabinettijohtajana ja maan kansallisen poliisin ylitarkastajana. Boyard vietiin torstaina Port-au-Princessä, ja tapausta pidetään viime vuosien korkea-arvoisimpana sieppauksena Haitissa, jossa jengiväkivalta on heikentänyt viranomaisten asemaa ja pahentanut turvallisuuskriisiä.

## Sieppaus tapahtui pääkaupungissa

Boyard siepattiin Port-au-Princen Bourdonin kaupunginosassa. Hän on korkea turvallisuusviranomainen ja laajasti arvostettu turvallisuusasiantuntija. Hän toimii puolustusministeri Mario Andrésolin esikuntapäällikkönä, ja Andrésol nimitettiin tehtäväänsä maaliskuussa.

Boyardin tehtäviin on kuulunut Haitin asevoimien uudelleenrakentamisen tukeminen. Hänen asemansa tekee tapauksesta poikkeuksellisen, sillä sieppauksen kohteena oli sekä puolustushallinnon että kansallisen poliisin korkea virkamies. Raporttien mukaan sieppauksen ovat vahvistaneet lähteisiinsä nojaten sekä uutistoimisto Associated Press että New York Times.

## Perhe vietiin mukana

Raporttien mukaan myös Boyardin vaimo ja kuusivuotias tytär vietiin sieppauksen yhteydessä. New York Timesin siteeraaman tapaukseen perehtyneen henkilön mukaan sieppaajat ovat esittäneet lunnasvaatimuksen. Julkisuuteen ei ole kerrottu, missä siepatut ovat tai millä ehdoilla heidät voitaisiin vapauttaa.

Haitissa sieppaukset ovat lisääntyneet rikollisryhmien laajentaessa vaikutusvaltaansa. Jengit ovat kiristäneet otettaan erityisesti pääkaupungissa, mikä on horjuttanut hallituksen auktoriteettia ja syventänyt maan humanitaarista ja turvallisuuskriisiä.

## Viranomaiset eivät ole kommentoineet toimia

Viranomaiset eivät ole julkisesti kertoneet, millaisia toimia Boyardin vapauttamiseksi on tehty. Tapaus on siksi edelleen ratkaisematta. Boyardin sieppausta pidetään merkittävänä kärjistymisenä, koska kohteena oli henkilö, jolla on keskeinen rooli maan turvallisuuskoneistossa ja asevoimien uudelleenrakentamiseen liittyvässä työssä.
summary_bullets: Boyard toimii puolustusministeriön kabinettijohtajana ja kansallisen poliisin ylitarkastajana.
Raporttien mukaan myös hänen vaimonsa ja kuusivuotias tyttärensä vietiin, ja tapauksessa on esitetty lunnasvaatimus.
